## Overview

Second PR of the split of #63232, stacked on #64111. Its base is `minimax-m31-flash-model`, so only this PR's commit shows up; it will be retargeted to `main` after #64111 merges. The change lets ROCm serve NVFP4-expert checkpoints such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: the routed experts are re-quantized to MXFP4/MXFP8 at load. It also makes fused shared experts (FSE) work with online quantization.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 MoE re-quantization without an NVFP4 backend:** main can already re-quantize serialized NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark) to an online MoE method. This PR makes that work where no NVFP4 MoE backend exists (ROCm):
  - The NVFP4 oracle skips backend selection for layers whose checkpoint method only serves as the dequantization source (`requantization_source_scope`).
  - `dequantize_weight` for MoE now yields `(experts, w13, w2)` per group of experts, which bounds the staging memory.
- **FSE with online quantization:** `OnlineSharedExpertLoader` stages the shared expert at load and quantizes it into its routed slot after loading. It replaces `RoutedExperts._fused_shared_expert_quantizer`, which only handled full-precision shared experts. Supported combinations:
  - NVFP4 routed experts re-quantized to MXFP4, with the shared expert re-quantized to the same scheme;
  - Quark MXFP4 routed experts (kept as stored) with an MXFP8 shared expert quantized to MXFP4 online.

  FSE is refused with a warning when the shared and routed experts would not run with the same `(weight, activation)` keys. Two cases raise `NotImplementedError`: BF16 routed experts quantized online combined with a quantized shared expert, and reloading weights with FSE.
- **MiniMax-M3 on ROCm:** a clear error for the NVFP4-expert checkpoint unless the routed experts are re-quantized (`--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` or `mxfp8`).
- **Two small ROCm fixes from the same branch:**
  - gfx942: the online FP8 PTPC MoE quantizes W13 in torch, because `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` can crash there during load.
  - The MXFP8 Triton activation quant uses a tuned block size for M == 1.

## Validation

Pre-commit passes, including mypy (Python 3.11) on all changed files.

Unit tests were run on GB300 (CUDA) for this branch and for #64111 (its base) in the same environment. The changed and new tests pass; the failures were identical on both branches (table below).

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py tests/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_emulation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

| | this PR | #64111 |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 656 | 646 |
| skipped | 86 | 54 |
| failed | 27 | 27 (the same tests) |

- The 10 extra passes are this PR's new tests.
- The 32 extra skips are the ROCm-only tests in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`.
- The 27 shared failures are environmental: engine start-up on GPUs shared with other jobs (about 10 GB free), a Triton "PTX compiled with an unsupported toolchain" error in this environment, and one out-of-memory error. Three `test_modelopt` failures also fail on `main` here.

Not covered:
- `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` holds most of the coverage of this PR (NVFP4 routed × online targets × FSE for compressed-tensors and Quark, Quark MXFP4 routed + MXFP8 shared, NVFP4 oracle skip). It is ROCm-only, and its CI jobs are disabled (`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`: pending locked torchao dependencies). I did not run it: there is no AMD hardware here.
- No ROCm end-to-end run on this branch. The code comes from the AMD contributors' branch (#63232).

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** #63547 (draft) also serves the NVFP4 M3.1 checkpoint on AMD, but converts NVFP4 → MXFP4 inside the model (`minimax_m3/common/nvfp4_mxfp4.py`). This PR goes through the generic online quantization API instead, so it applies to any ModelOpt, compressed-tensors or Quark NVFP4 MoE and supports FSE.
- **Shared code touched (all at load time, no forward-path change):**
  - `resolve_quant_method` builds the checkpoint method of re-quantized experts under `requantization_source_scope`.
  - `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` returns the emulation backend inside that scope.
  - `QuantizeMethodBase.dequantize_weight` returns an iterator for MoE. All three MoE implementations (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark NVFP4) and the one caller are migrated.
  - `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` and `load_weights` route shared-expert slots through the loader.
  - `process_weights_after_loading` finalizes the staged shared experts. It is a no-op unless FSE and online quantization are both used.
  - `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` now compares the effective `(weight, activation)` keys of the routed and shared experts.
  - `QuarkLinearMethod.dequantize_weight` supports MXFP8.
- **Conflicts with main:** main's #61457 (per-layer FSE selection) landed after the source branch. I kept main's `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert`. The source branch's extra warning, for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` set without AITER MoE, was dropped: it also fires on CUDA, where AITER is unavailable.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/quantization/online.md` already documents NVFP4 MoE re-quantization; FSE with online quantization is not documented yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes from #63232 and resolve the conflicts with main. The original code is by fxmarty-amd (re-quantization + FSE), andyluo7 (gfx942 FP8) and hongxiayang (MXFP8 M=1), credited in the commit. The submitter reviewed the port and ran the tests above.

This is with a fix to `test_fse_online_quantization_routed_shared_loads_checkpoint_weights`, which fails on the current branch head:

```
vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/model.py:1833: in get_expert_mapping
E       AttributeError: 'ModelStub' object has no attribute 'fused_shared_expert_layers'. Did you mean: 'is_fused_shared_expert_enabled'?
```

Since per-layer FSE (#61457, merged from main), `MiniMaxM3Model.load_weights` redirects a checkpoint shared expert into its routed slot only when `rocm_aiter_ops.is_fusion_moe_shared_experts_enabled()` and `extract_layer_index(name) in self.fused_shared_expert_layers`. The test stub was written for the former model-level `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled` bool. The fix:
- set `fused_shared_expert_layers = frozenset({0})` on the stub instead of `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled = True`;
- name the checkpoint weights `layers.0.block_sparse_moe....` and register the experts under `model.layers[0]`, so the layer index can be parsed;
- enable the global AITER FSE gate only around `load_weights` (monkeypatch). Enabling AITER MoE for the whole test would also switch the expert kernels, and their weight layout, that the test compares against.

The new tests also took ~43s, almost all in full `gc.collect()` calls: the autouse `cleanup_fixture` teardown (~0.4s per test) and the two calls in `BaseModelLoader.load_model` (~0.8s per loading test). The model work itself is ~25 ms per test. The pure unit tests of this PR (no distributed state, no model) are now marked `skip_global_cleanup`, which brings the run to ~27s.

## End-to-end: `vllm serve` combinations on MI355X

Commands for the routed / shared expert online requantization combinations supported by this PR, on the base models:
- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`: NVFP4 routed experts, MXFP8 shared experts.
- `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: MXFP4 routed experts, MXFP8 shared experts.

FSE (fused shared experts) is enabled with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` (default `0`). `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` defaults to `1`.

This is tested on MI355X, TP4.

Common arguments, from the [MI355X recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash?hardware=mi355x):

```bash
COMMON_ARGS=(
  --block-size 128
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
  --tensor-parallel-size 4
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "indexer_decode_cp": true}'
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
)
```

### `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (NVFP4 routed)

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP4
- shared expert MXFP8 -> MXFP4
- FSE enabled

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp4", "*shared_expert*": "mxfp4"}'
```

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP8
- Shared expert not re-quantized
- no FSE

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp8"}'
```

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP4
- Shared expert not re-quantized
- no FSE

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp4"}'
```

### `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` (MXFP4 routed)

Re-quantized online: shared expert MXFP8 -> MXFP4 (routed experts already MXFP4), fused (FSE):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*shared_expert*": "mxfp4"}'
```

With FSE and online quantization, the logs show for example (Quark checkpoint):

```
[base_loader.py:151] Quantizing 114 layers of types: block_sparse_moe.shared_experts.down_proj: 57 (from targets: *shared_expert*, mxfp4); 
block_sparse_moe.shared_experts.gate_up_proj: 57 (from targets: *shared_expert*, mxfp4)
[utils.py:563] AITER fused shared experts: enabled on MoE layer(s) [3, 4, 5, ...]
```

### Accuracy sanity check (GSM8K)

GSM8K platinum, 5-shot, 5 repeats, against each server above. Sampling uses the server defaults from `generation_config.json` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95). The model thinks by default; with `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3` the trace is returned in `reasoning_content`, so `content` has no end-of-thinking marker (`think_end_token=''`).

**Please note that this is sanity check only, I am not making claim about either of the re-quantization quality.**

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
    --model_args "model=<server-model-id>,base_url=http://<server-ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=128,timeout=99999,tokenized_requests=False,think_end_token='',tokenizer=<server-model-id>,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,server_sampling_defaults=True" \
    --tasks gsm8k_platinum \
    --num_fewshot 5 \
    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=8000" \
    --repeats 5 \
    --log_samples --output_path results \
    --apply_chat_template \
    --generation-length
```

This uses the `lm-eval-fixes` branch of https://github.com/fxmarty-amd/lm-evaluation-harness, which provides `--repeats` statistics, `think_end_token`, `server_sampling_defaults` and `--generation-length`.

### Results

GSM8K platinum, 5-shot, 5 repeats, `max_gen_toks=8000`, on branch commit 60a282ab89, MI355 TP4 with the `COMMON_ARGS` above. Metrics use the `flexible-extract` filter: mean@5 is lm-eval's `exact_match_mean_repeats`; maj@5 is the majority vote over the 5 extracted answers per question. Tokens per answer are the server-reported `completion_tokens` (reasoning included).

detail.body:
## Overview

Second PR of the split of #63232, stacked on #64111. Its base is `minimax-m31-flash-model`, so only this PR's commit shows up; it will be retargeted to `main` after #64111 merges. The change lets ROCm serve NVFP4-expert checkpoints such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: the routed experts are re-quantized to MXFP4/MXFP8 at load. It also makes fused shared experts (FSE) work with online quantization.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 MoE re-quantization without an NVFP4 backend:** main can already re-quantize serialized NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark) to an online MoE method. This PR makes that work where no NVFP4 MoE backend exists (ROCm):
  - The NVFP4 oracle skips backend selection for layers whose checkpoint method only serves as the dequantization source (`requantization_source_scope`).
  - `dequantize_weight` for MoE now yields `(experts, w13, w2)` per group of experts, which bounds the staging memory.
- **FSE with online quantization:** `OnlineSharedExpertLoader` stages the shared expert at load and quantizes it into its routed slot after loading. It replaces `RoutedExperts._fused_shared_expert_quantizer`, which only handled full-precision shared experts. Supported combinations:
  - NVFP4 routed experts re-quantized to MXFP4, with the shared expert re-quantized to the same scheme;
  - Quark MXFP4 routed experts (kept as stored) with an MXFP8 shared expert quantized to MXFP4 online.

  FSE is refused with a warning when the shared and routed experts would not run with the same `(weight, activation)` keys. Two cases raise `NotImplementedError`: BF16 routed experts quantized online combined with a quantized shared expert, and reloading weights with FSE.
- **MiniMax-M3 on ROCm:** a clear error for the NVFP4-expert checkpoint unless the routed experts are re-quantized (`--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` or `mxfp8`).
- **Two small ROCm fixes from the same branch:**
  - gfx942: the online FP8 PTPC MoE quantizes W13 in torch, because `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` can crash there during load.
  - The MXFP8 Triton activation quant uses a tuned block size for M == 1.

## Validation

Pre-commit passes, including mypy (Python 3.11) on all changed files.

Unit tests were run on GB300 (CUDA) for this branch and for #64111 (its base) in the same environment. The changed and new tests pass; the failures were identical on both branches (table below).

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py tests/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_emulation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

| | this PR | #64111 |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 656 | 646 |
| skipped | 86 | 54 |
| failed | 27 | 27 (the same tests) |

- The 10 extra passes are this PR's new tests.
- The 32 extra skips are the ROCm-only tests in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`.
- The 27 shared failures are environmental: engine start-up on GPUs shared with other jobs (about 10 GB free), a Triton "PTX compiled with an unsupported toolchain" error in this environment, and one out-of-memory error. Three `test_modelopt` failures also fail on `main` here.

Not covered:
- `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` holds most of the coverage of this PR (NVFP4 routed × online targets × FSE for compressed-tensors and Quark, Quark MXFP4 routed + MXFP8 shared, NVFP4 oracle skip). It is ROCm-only, and its CI jobs are disabled (`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`: pending locked torchao dependencies). I did not run it: there is no AMD hardware here.
- No ROCm end-to-end run on this branch. The code comes from the AMD contributors' branch (#63232).

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** #63547 (draft) also serves the NVFP4 M3.1 checkpoint on AMD, but converts NVFP4 → MXFP4 inside the model (`minimax_m3/common/nvfp4_mxfp4.py`). This PR goes through the generic online quantization API instead, so it applies to any ModelOpt, compressed-tensors or Quark NVFP4 MoE and supports FSE.
- **Shared code touched (all at load time, no forward-path change):**
  - `resolve_quant_method` builds the checkpoint method of re-quantized experts under `requantization_source_scope`.
  - `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` returns the emulation backend inside that scope.
  - `QuantizeMethodBase.dequantize_weight` returns an iterator for MoE. All three MoE implementations (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark NVFP4) and the one caller are migrated.
  - `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` and `load_weights` route shared-expert slots through the loader.
  - `process_weights_after_loading` finalizes the staged shared experts. It is a no-op unless FSE and online quantization are both used.
  - `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` now compares the effective `(weight, activation)` keys of the routed and shared experts.
  - `QuarkLinearMethod.dequantize_weight` supports MXFP8.
- **Conflicts with main:** main's #61457 (per-layer FSE selection) landed after the source branch. I kept main's `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert`. The source branch's extra warning, for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` set without AITER MoE, was dropped: it also fires on CUDA, where AITER is unavailable.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/quantization/online.md` already documents NVFP4 MoE re-quantization; FSE with online quantization is not documented yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes from #63232 and resolve the conflicts with main. The original code is by fxmarty-amd (re-quantization + FSE), andyluo7 (gfx942 FP8) and hongxiayang (MXFP8 M=1), credited in the commit. The submitter reviewed the port and ran the tests above.

+    quantization.
+
+    - Staged shared experts: the shared experts are loaded as stored in temporary
+      slots (``online_w{13,2}_weight[_scale]``), dequantized after loading, and
+      quantized into the routed experts slots: with the routed experts when they
+      are requantized, else by ``finalize``.
+    - Unquantized shared experts with pre-quantized routed experts: the shared
+      experts are quantized on arrival by ``quantizer``, and loaded in the routed
+      experts slots.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        quant_config,
+        online_config,
+        quant_method: Any,
+        shared_expert_prefix: str | None,
+        num_logical_experts: int,
+        num_fused_shared_experts: int,
+    ):
+        self.shared_expert_prefix = shared_expert_prefix
+        self.num_logical_experts = num_logical_experts
+        self.num_fused_shared_experts = num_fused_shared_experts
+        # The routed experts are requantized online from their checkpoint format.
+        self.routed_requantized = (
+            isinstance(quant_method, OnlineRequantizationMixin)
+            and quant_method.requantization_source is not None
+        )
+        # Requantized routed experts quantize the staged shared experts with them.
+        self.stages_shared_experts = self.routed_requantized

+        target_key = self._get_shared_target_key(online_config)

+                quant_config, f"{shared_expert_prefix}.down_proj", LinearBase
+            )[0]
+        if (
+            not self.routed_requantized
+            and target_key is not None
+            and self.stored_key != target_key
+        ):
+            from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.online.base import (
+                ONLINE_SHARED_EXPERT_QUANTIZERS,
+            )
+
+            if target_key not in ONLINE_SHARED_EXPERT_QUANTIZERS:
+                raise NotImplementedError(

+                    "open an issue."
+                )
+            self.quantizer = ONLINE_SHARED_EXPERT_QUANTIZERS[target_key]
+            # Quantized shared experts are staged, as their weight and scale
+            # are needed together to be dequantized.
+            self.stages_shared_experts = self.stored_key is not None

+                OnlineMoEMethodBase,

+            if self.stages_shared_experts and isinstance(

+                    "with routed experts quantized online from high "
+                    "precision. Disable FSE or open an issue."

- set `fused_shared_expert_layers = frozenset({0})` on the stub instead of `is_fused_shared_expert_enabled = True`;
- name the checkpoint weights `layers.0.block_sparse_moe....` and register the experts under `model.layers[0]`, so the layer index can be parsed;
- enable the global AITER FSE gate only around `load_weights` (monkeypatch). Enabling AITER MoE for the whole test would also switch the expert kernels, and their weight layout, that the test compares against.

## End-to-end: `vllm serve` combinations on MI355X

Commands for the routed / shared expert online requantization combinations supported by this PR, on the base models:
- `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`: NVFP4 routed experts, MXFP8 shared experts.
- `amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4`: MXFP4 routed experts, MXFP8 shared experts.

FSE (fused shared experts) is enabled with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` (default `0`). `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE` defaults to `1`.

This is tested on MI355X, TP4.

Common arguments, from the [MI355X recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash?hardware=mi355x):

```bash
COMMON_ARGS=(
  --block-size 128
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
  --tensor-parallel-size 4
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "indexer_decode_cp": true}'
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}'
)
```

### `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (NVFP4 routed)

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP4
- shared expert MXFP8 -> MXFP4
- FSE enabled

```bash

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp4", "*shared_expert*": "mxfp4"}'
```

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP8
- Shared expert not re-quantized
- no FSE

```bash

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp8"}'
```

Re-quantized online:
- routed experts NVFP4 -> MXFP4
- Shared expert not re-quantized
- no FSE

```bash

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    "${COMMON_ARGS[@]}" \
    --quantization-config.targets '{"*block_sparse_moe.experts*": "mxfp4"}'
```

Re-quantized online: shared expert MXFP8 -> MXFP4 (routed experts already MXFP4), fused (FSE):


### Accuracy sanity check (GSM8K)

GSM8K platinum, 5-shot, 5 repeats, against each server above. Sampling uses the server defaults from `generation_config.json` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95). The model thinks by default; with `--reasoning-parser minimax_m3` the trace is returned in `reasoning_content`, so `content` has no end-of-thinking marker (`think_end_token=''`).

**Please note that this is sanity check only, I am not making claim about either of the re-quantization quality.**

```bash

    --model_args "model=<server-model-id>,base_url=http://<server-ip>:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=128,timeout=99999,tokenized_requests=False,think_end_token='',tokenizer=<server-model-id>,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,server_sampling_defaults=True" \

    --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=8000" \
    --repeats 5 \
    --log_samples --output_path results \
    --apply_chat_template \
    --generation-length
```
